extracted.intended_audience: constitutional framers, political leaders, and engaged citizens interested in constitutional design (late-18th-century American context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing a constitutional structure: the separation and balance of legislative, executive, and judicial powers, representation rules, and federal vs. state checks. Focuses on what features preserve liberty and efficient government and warns against concentrations of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three branches of power (necessity and balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three branches of power have an unalterable foundation in nature; if all of them are not acknowledged in any constitution of government, it will be found to be imperfect, unliable, and soon enslaved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay repeatedly argues that a mixture of three powers in a commonwealth produces the fairest prospects for liberty and good government (example: Rome and England as mixed governments). The absence of complete independence in each branch or an ineffectual balance produces domestic contests and revolutions. Use the three-branch structure as a baseline when designing constitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of legislative and executive authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislative and executive authorities are naturally distinct; liberty and the laws depend entirely on a separation of them in the frame of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not vest legislative and executive powers in the same body. Historical examples and thought experiments show that combining them produces confusion, delay, and opens the way for domination of one power over another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive negative (veto) to defend against legislative encroachment
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislative power is naturally and necessarily sovereign and supreme over the executive; and therefore the latter must be made an essential branch of the former, even with a negative, or it will be invaded, undermined, attacked, or in some way totally ruined and annihilated by the former.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give negatives (veto powers) to governors/executives to protect the executive branch from legislative encroachment. The necessity of a negative in the house of representatives is asserted as virtually unquestionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal deputies must be accountable to states; states serve as checks
rubrics_metrics.description: In confederacies the deputies are responsible to the states; their authority is clearly ascertained; and the states, in their separate capacities, are the checks. The security against the dangers of a single-council government depends upon the accuracy and decision with which the governments of the separate states have their own orders arranged and balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing a federal government with a single federal assembly, ensure deputies' responsibilities to their state governments and clear state-level checks; the federal arrangement's safety depends on well-ordered and balanced state governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: At least one essential branch must be subject to frequent popular elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular elections of one essential branch of the legislature, frequently repeated, are the only possible method of forming a free constitution, or of preferring the government of laws from the domination of men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that at least one legislative branch is directly and frequently answerable to the people to maintain liberty. This is presented as the central safeguard against the consolidation of power and the loss of public liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation design: small districts, frequent elections, local residency
rubrics_metrics.description: If county-members were abolished, and representatives proportionally and frequently chosen in small districts, and if no candidate could be chosen but an established long-settled inhabitant of that district, it would be impossible to corrupt the people of England, and the house of commons might be an immortal guardian of the national liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design electoral districts small and local, require long-settled inhabitants as candidates, and hold frequent elections to reduce corruption, patronage, and aristocratic influence over representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct and constant communication between people and legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberty of the people depends entirely on the constant and direct communication between them and the legislature, by means of their representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize channels (frequent elections, local districts, accountable representatives) that keep lawmakers directly tied to constituents; removing this connection risks tyranny by deputies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentrating all powers in a single assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: A single assembly possessing all authority—legislative, executive, and judicial—will be impracticable: appointment of officers, management of military and diplomatic posts, administration of justice, etc., would overwhelm the assembly, causing confusion, delay, corruption, and aristocratic control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give one body sole power over appointments, military command, administration, and trials; separate executive functions (appointments, administration) and judicial functions (trials) to specialized branches to ensure efficiency and protect rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive appointment authority for efficient administration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an assembly is to appoint generals, admirals, ambassadors, and all other officers, the business would fill the whole year and be more than could be done—information must be had and the assembly must be informed before it can act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign appointment powers for military, naval, revenue, customs, police, justice, and foreign ministers to an executive (or an executive-dependent mechanism) rather than a large legislative assembly to avoid perpetual delay and patronage-driven selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemblies are unfit as primary criminal tribunals
rubrics_metrics.description: Shall every criminal be brought before this assembly and tried? Shall he be there accused before five hundred men? Witnesses introduced, counsel heard? This again would take up more than the whole year; and no man, after all, would consider his life, liberty, or property safe in such a tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make the legislative assembly the primary criminal court; establish a separate judiciary with competent judges and procedures to secure fair trials and protect rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of perpetual or life senates and aristocratic executive control
rubrics_metrics.description: Milton's scheme of a grand council perpetual and Hume's plan of senators holding executive power are dangerous; perpetual councils or senates for life tend to oligarchy and would deprive people and their representatives of legislative voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lifetime or perpetual legislative bodies that accumulate executive power; these arrangements tend toward aristocratic domination, corruption, and the erosion of popular representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual design of federal powers (comparative & local conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To collect together the ancient and modern leagues ... and compare them all, with the circumstances, the situation, the geography, the commerce, the population, and the forms of government, as well as the climate, the soil, and manners of the people, and consider what further federal powers are wanted, and may be safely given, would be a useful work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding what powers to grant to a federal government, conduct comparative study of historical confederacies and analyze local geographic, economic, demographic, and cultural conditions before assigning federal authorities.
